title: Joan Miró's birth chart
metaDescription: Joan Miró's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 0.6° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Fixed signs carry three of the nine placements whose signs are settled — the broadest certain weighting in the chart. Fixed weight is the scheme’s deep keel: slow to turn, near-impossible to capsize.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 0.6° Taurus — deep enough in the first decan (0°–10°) that Venus, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 5.9° Aries, Venus was at 27.5° Aries, Mars was at 14.8° Gemini. Read together: thought that arrives already in motion; attraction declared rather than implied; effort aimed through strategy and words.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Saturn trine Pluto, 0.6° of separation. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, Neptune conjunction Pluto at 1.1°, and Saturn trine Neptune at 1.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags two placements in this chart. Venus in Aries at 27.5° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Libra at 7.8° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 4 in air, 2 in earth, 2 in fire, 1 in water by element, 3 fixed, 3 cardinal, 3 mutable by modality. Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Gemini into Cancer during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.6° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
